blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines— The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has rejected former President Rodrigo Duterte‘s request to require expert verification of evidence sourced from open platforms, saying the proposed process could unnecessarily delay the start of his trial. In a Sept. 28 decision, the chamber denied the defense’s bid to amend the ICC’s “E-Court Protocol” to impose stricter authentication requirements for open-source and user-generated materials in Duterte’s crimes against humanity case.
